name: Arrow Root Blanc-Mange
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: juice and grated peel of 1 lemon
ingredients.originalText: juice and grated peel of 1 lemon

ingredients.name: 1 1/2 pints of very rich milk or cream
ingredients.originalText: 1 1/2 pints of very rich milk or cream
ingredients.quantityText: 1 1/2 pints of very rich milk or cream

instructions.text: Take a tea-cup full of arrow root, put it into a large bowl, and dissolve it in a little cold water.
When it is melted, pour off the water, and let the arrow root remain undisturbed.
Boil in half a pint of unskimmed milk, made very sweet with white sugar, a beaten nutmeg, and eight or nine blades of mace, mixed with the juice and grated peel of a lemon.
When it has boiled long enough to be highly flavoured, strain it into a pint and a half of very rich milk or cream, and add a quarter of a pound of sugar.
Boil the whole for ten minutes; then strain it, boiling hot, over the arrow root.
Stir it well and frequently till cold; then put it into moulds and let it set to congeal.

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Take a tea-cup full of arrow root, put it into a large bowl, and dissolve it in a little cold water.
2. When it is melted, pour off the water, and let the arrow root remain undisturbed.
3. Boil in half a pint of unskimmed milk, made very sweet with white sugar, a beaten nutmeg, and eight or nine blades of mace, mixed with the juice and grated peel of a lemon.
4. When it has boiled long enough to be highly flavoured, strain it into a pint and a half of very rich milk or cream, and add a quarter of a pound of sugar.
5. Boil the whole for ten minutes; then strain it, boiling hot, over the arrow root.
6. Stir it well and frequently till cold; then put it into moulds and let it set to congeal.
